page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a bare metal server configured with an Intel Xeon 2288G processor operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this dedicated server features 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) via hyperthreading. The hardware includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server is equipped with a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this system.

Benchmark evaluations indicate balanced performance across standard computing tasks. The server achieves average-tier results in stress-ng single-core (2024.2) and multi-core (19837.37) CPU tests, as well as in Geekbench single-core (1789.0) and multi-core (8643.0) assessments. Notably, the system demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in data compression, with gzip compression reaching 36.22 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.23 GB/sec. While the Passmark memory score is in the top tier at 3594.89, large-block uncached memory bandwidth tests show weaker performance, with read speeds at 29.76 GB/sec and write speeds at 15.32 GB/sec.

With its dedicated CPU allocation, 128.0 GB of RAM, and 3840 GB of local NVMe storage, this server is well-suited for database hosting, static web serving, and software compilation. It handles Redis SET operations at an average rate of 17.28 million operations per second and static web serving at 11.49 GB/sec. However, the system is less optimal for larger machine learning workloads; while small 135M LLM inference is average, medium 7B LLM inference drops to a weak tier, and large 70B models are unsupported due to the lack of GPU acceleration.
